t: Historians disagree whether the khanate began in 1437 or 1438, when Ulugh Muhammad took power in Kazan, or in 1445, when his son Maxmud began to rule there.
From 1487 to 1521 the khanate was in effect a Muscovite protectorate, and its nobility was split between pro-Moscow and pro-Crimean groups.
Ivan the Terrible's forces stormed Kazan on 2 October 1552 after a siege of more than 40 days, and most of the defenders were killed and the population massacred.
dyk: No document of the khanate survived the Russian conquest, and the records of the early Russian administration of Kazan were destroyed during the Time of Troubles.
ev: Ulugh Muhammad, a former khan of the Golden Horde, takes power in Kazan with the support of the local nobility
Maxmud and his brother Yakub defeat the army of Vasily II of Moscow near Suzdal and capture him
Ivan III of Moscow occupies Kazan and places Möxämmädämin on the throne
The Crimean prince Sahib Giray takes the Kazan throne and leads a campaign against Moscow
Pro-Moscow nobles rise in the Kazan uprising and depose Safa Giray
The Kazan nobility accepts Russian terms, giving up the lands west of the Volga
Russian forces storm Kazan after a siege of more than 40 days
The Mari stop resisting Russian rule in the former khanate

f.founder: Ulugh Muhammad (1437 or 1438) or his son Maxmud (1445); historians disagree
f.predecessor: Golden Horde; the Kazan Ulus of former Volga Bulgaria
f.successor: Tsardom of Russia (the Tsardom of Kazan, later the Kazan Governorate)
